_doc: Effort model v2 (hours; days = hours / hours_per_day). Code work is costed as manual-equivalent hours and then multiplied by the AI-assistance factor (AWS Transform for .NET, GitHub Copilot app modernization, coding agents). QA, cut-over, infrastructure and coordination are costed separately and only partly accelerated. Every number is a [low, high] range; 'likely' = low + 40% of the range. Calibrate from your own actuals here, never in code. See references/estimation-model.md.

ai_assistance._doc: Share of manual-equivalent effort that remains when work is tool/agent-assisted. code: AWS Transform for .NET / GitHub Copilot app modernization / coding agents do the mechanical port (AWS cites up to 4x); engineers direct, review and fix. qa: AI-generated characterisation/regression tests and automated runs; sign-off and UAT stay human. ops: IaC/pipeline templates generated and reviewed. db: AWS DMS Schema Conversion (generative AI) / SCT plus agents for T-SQL to PL/pgSQL. Set enabled=false for a manual estimate.

conversion_hours_per_kloc._doc: Manual-equivalent hours per 1,000 hand-written lines (C#/VB; generated code excluded) to port a project to SDK-style + target .NET; markup has its own rate (markup_hours_per_kloc). Findings marked baseline are inside these rates.

conversion_fixed_hours._doc: Manual-equivalent hours per project: project file, packages, build, smoke test.

finding_hours._doc: Manual-equivalent remediation hours per finding: fixed + per extra occurrence, capped. Findings with baseline=true are already inside the conversion rate.

qa_hours._doc: Testing per application (functional regression, UAT support): fixed + per KLOC; more when the repository has fewer than 2 test methods per KLOC. Scales with functionality, not with code-change speed. Above full_rate_kloc of hand-written code the per-KLOC rate is multiplied by beyond_rate_factor (test effort follows features, not lines).

operations_hours._doc: Per deployable application: container image, pipeline, configuration/secrets, cut-over and hypercare. Estate-level foundation (landing zone, networking, CI/CD, observability) once per assessment.

database_hours._doc: Per database: schema + data migration and rehearsal (blocker fixes added from findings).

multipliers._doc: Applied on top of work-package hours.

parallel_dev_drift._doc: by commits per week in the activity window

hosting_scenarios._doc: Client hosting preference applied to every server application (desktop clients and retired apps keep their decision). skip_categories: findings not needed in that scenario.

modernize.label: Modernize: .NET 10 on Linux containers (ECS Fargate) with managed AWS services

linux-lift.label: Lift-and-shift to EC2 Linux: minimal port to .NET 10, same architecture (Kestrel + nginx/systemd, single host or ASG)
linux-lift.blocked_note: Applications with a Windows-bound blocker (Web Forms, COM, desktop UI ...) cannot run on Linux without a rewrite: they are rehosted on EC2 Windows in this scenario.

windows-rehost.label: Rehost as-is on EC2 Windows (lift-and-shift, no code port)

database_scenarios._doc: Database target applied to every database group.
database_scenarios.rds-sqlserver: Amazon RDS for SQL Server (lift-and-shift of the database)
database_scenarios.babelfish: Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish (T-SQL kept, SQL Server licence removed)
database_scenarios.postgresql: Full port to PostgreSQL (Aurora PostgreSQL / RDS PostgreSQL): schema, T-SQL code and data access converted
database_scenarios.dual: Dual support: the application runs on both SQL Server and PostgreSQL
database_scenarios.ec2-sqlserver: SQL Server on EC2 (licence retained, full control)

postgres._doc: Manual-equivalent hours for porting SQL Server objects and data access to PostgreSQL (before db_factor).

dual.note: Both providers must stay in sync: provider-neutral data access (EF Core with provider-specific migrations, no T-SQL in code), every procedure maintained twice or moved into the application, and every release tested on both databases.

markup_hours_per_kloc._doc: Views / pages (cshtml, aspx, ascx, master, xaml): far less change than C# when the UI stack stays; Web Forms markup is rewritten.
